prerequisites: Basic knowledge of industrial design for the representation of mechanical components
Knowledge of the main elements of machines
Basics of materials mechanics (elastic modulus, yield strength, Poisson's ratio)

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire a solid understanding of the fundamental principles and parametric modeling techniques necessary for the creation, verification, and management of industrial products.
Acquire knowledge related to digital product management using 3D geometric modeling software (Autodesk Inventor) and finite element analysis (Ansys Workbench).
Acquire the skills necessary to work with Autodesk Inventor and Ansys Workbench programs, create 3D models, and understand how to modify them parametrically to improve their mechanical behavior.
Digitally model mechanical components and assemblies, verifying their mechanical performance through Ansys Workbench.
Analyze and verify the mechanical performance of modeled components.
Communicate the results obtained to various company stakeholders (e.g., R&D, Marketing) through the production of technical and product documentation (e.g., bill of materials, reports).

syllabus_topics: Introduction to finite element analysis (theoretical overview)
Introduction to Ansys Workbench: analysis workflow (e.g., modeling, element selection, mechanical properties, loads, constraints)
Technical documentation: interpreting results and generating reports
teaching_methods: Classroom exercises in the computer lab

assessment_methods.method: CAD modeling of a “mobile” mechanism and related assembly (project)
Finite element analysis of one or more components of the modeled assembly (project)
Project report and related technical documentation

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a project with two equally weighted parts: CAD modeling (15/30) and finite element analysis (15/30). Students are evaluated based on the project report and technical documentation. It is possible to integrate the project evaluation with an oral exam or submit a new project involving a new mechanism and component.
